findings.title: AC 5 conflicts with spec test-import rule
findings.problem: AC 5 forbids any module importing an underscore name from a router-defining module, yet Scope keeps _resolve_effective_llm_model, _enrich_toolkit_settings_config, _create_settings_config_lookup, _filter_invalid_datasources, _ask_assistant_resume and _resume_tool_call in route modules and the test rule says imports take the defining submodule. Tests (test_assistant.py, test_assistant_filter_invalid_datasources.py, test_tool_call_resume.py, test_toolkit_settings_config.py) import them from assistant.catalog, .management and .execution, so AC 5 as written is partially unmet.
findings.impact: Shipping as is leaves a required criterion partially unmet. Satisfying it literally would change Scope and break the byte-identical move, so the intended rule needs a human call.
findings.recommendation: Human decision needed: either scope AC 5 to src/ (tests then keep importing underscore helpers from their defining route module, as the spec's test rule says), or move those helpers into a private module and re-point the tests. Record the outcome in spec.md.

findings.title: Public helper lacks return annotation
findings.problem: check_user_can_access_assistant, made public by this change, annotates its parameters but declares no return type; code-quality.md requires explicit parameter and return types on public functions.
findings.impact: Documented typing standard is broken on a helper now shared across routers and services; the standards audit marks it workflow-blocking. Reachability is static: the function is defined and called from the moved routers.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the return type: def check_user_can_access_assistant(user: User, assistant: Assistant, action_name: str, action_type: Action) -> None:
